1.note: Common term on Korean construction sites; 현장소장 is the site manager, a different role.
Informal site term for an assistant or general laborer.

1.en: Good morning, team. Everyone is here.

2.en: Today we are working on the scaffold on the east side.
The main hazard is falling objects from above.
Everyone must wear a hard hat and safety glasses.
Please keep clear of the forklift route.
Does anyone have questions about the emergency plan?
2.es: 비상 대응 계획에 대해 질문 있으신 분 계십니까?

3.en: Can you bring me the drill and some screws?

4.note: Generic term for cut wood used in construction.
Casual: 납품 is more formal on invoices.

4.en: I need 20 boards of 2x4, 8 feet long.
I also need 50 pounds of 3-inch nails.
How many sheets of plywood do you have in stock?
Can you deliver the rebar by Thursday morning?
4.es: 철근을 목요일 오전까지 배송해 주실 수 있습니까?

5.en: The wall runs from point A to point B.
5.es: 벽은 A 지점에서 B 지점까지 갑니다.

5.en: The door is 1.2 meters from the corner.
Start the chalk line on the north wall.
Check the measurement against the blueprint.

6.en: Hold the stud steady while I nail it.
6.es: 제가 못 박는 동안 스터드 잡아 주세요.

6.en: Check the level before you nail.
Watch out, the saw is moving.
Cut it to the marked line.
Wear your hard hat over the framing area.

7.en: Install the OSB on the roof, starting from the eave.
7.note: Polite formal -ㅂ니다 style, suitable for addressing a crew or site meeting.

7.en: Lay the felt first, then the drip edge.
7.es: 펠트를 먼저 깔고 물끊기 몰딩을 설치하세요.
7.note: Polite -세요 instruction style used by foremen with crew.

7.en: Start the shingles from the ridge and work down.
Check the rafters before you cover them.

8.en: Fill the form up to the mark.

8.note: In practice, levelling is usually done with a screed or straightedge; vibrators consolidate concrete. Confirm your crew's method.

8.en: Cover it and keep it wet for seven days.
8.es: 덮어 두고 7일 동안 습하게 유지해 주세요.
8.note: Confirm the curing period with the project spec or engineer.

9.note: Polite form (-세요); a common way to start a problem report.

9.en: When did you notice the problem?
What did you do after that?
Are you hurt? Is anyone injured?
9.note: Ask about people first, before anything else.

9.en: Good. Now stop work in this area.
9.es: 좋아요. 이제 이 구역 작업을 중단하세요.

9.en: I'll check the blueprint and call you back.

10.en: The slab is eight feet six inches long.
10.note: Korean uses 피트 and 인치 on construction sites; numbers are Sino-Korean for feet/inches (8피트 6인치).

10.en: Please check the wall is twelve feet by ten feet.
10.note: Use 'x' spoken as 곱하기 or '×' in writing; 'by' is common in site talk.

10.en: What is the area of this room?
Is the scaffold height under twenty feet?
10.note: Polite spoken form; use 요 for crew members in casual settings, 습니다 for formal briefings.

10.en: Can you repeat that measurement, please?
10.note: Polite request to a subcontractor; use 주시겠어요 for respect.

11.en: We start rebar tying at 8 o'clock.
11.note: Formal polite register (-ㅂ니다), standard on job sites.
Use 전에 for 'before' with a time.
Short and clear for crew announcements.

11.en: If we finish early, we can pour the concrete.
11.es: 일찍 끝나면 콘크리트를 타설할 수 있습니다.
11.note: Conditional 면 is the everyday way to say 'if' here.
Korean uses 시 for hours and 분 for minutes.

11.en: Please finish cleanup before we leave.

12.en: Don't touch any wire until I confirm the power is off.
12.es: 전원이 꺼졌다고 확인하기 전까지 전선 만지지 마세요.
12.note: Direct, safety-critical; use 해요체 or 반말 only with close crew.

12.en: Lock out the panel before you start pulling wire.
12.es: 배선 작업 시작 전에 분전반에 잠금장치를 거세요.
12.note: Standard crew-level instruction in Korean job sites.

12.en: Everyone, put on insulated gloves and safety glasses first.
12.es: 여러분, 먼저 절연 장갑이랑 보안경 착용하세요.

12.en: Test with the voltage tester before you touch anything.
Report any damaged cord to me right away.
Who is responsible for the lockout tags today?

13.en: Hang the panel first, then screw it into the studs.
13.es: 패널을 먼저 달고 스터드에 나사로 고정하세요.

13.en: Are the screws spaced every 8 inches?
13.note: Use 인치 for inches; confirm the spec on the plans.

13.en: Apply tape and compound over every joint.
Let the compound dry before you sand it.
Is the primer ready for the texture coat?
13.es: 프라이머가 질감 마감 작업을 할 준비가 되었나요?

14.en: This is not right. Please fix it this way.
14.es: 이거 잘못됐어요. 이렇게 다시 해 주세요.

14.en: Please check the blueprint before you continue.
The rebar spacing must match the drawing.
Please wear your hard hat at all times.
Let's fix this before the inspection.

15.en: Do you have experience in concrete work?

15.es: 다음 주 월요일부터 시작하실 수 있나요?

15.en: The pay is 200,000 won per day.
Could you give me the names of two references?
15.es: 추천인 두 분의 연락처를 알려 주시겠어요?

15.en: Please wear your hard hat and safety vest at all times.
15.es: 현장에서는 항상 안전모와 안전 조끼를 착용해 주세요.

15.en: Start time is 7:30, and parking is over there.
15.es: 시작 시간은 7시 30분이고, 주차는 저쪽에 하시면 됩니다.

16.en: Hello, I'm the foreman from the general contractor.
16.note: Polite standard form; use 입니다 for formal calls to a sub's supervisor.

16.en: Can your crew be here Monday at seven?
16.es: 월요일 7시에 귀사 팀이 오실 수 있을까요?
16.note: Use 귀사 for the other company; 팀 is common in crew talk.

16.en: Please finish the rebar before the concrete pour.
16.es: 콘크리트 타설 전에 철근 작업을 끝내 주세요.
16.note: 주세요 is polite but direct; softer option: 부탁드려도 될까요?

16.en: When can you confirm the deadline?
16.es: 마감 기한을 언제 확인해 주실 수 있을까요?

16.en: Please check the scaffold before the inspection.

17.en: I'd like to place an order for 50 sheets of plywood.
17.note: Formal polite register, suitable for calling a supplier.

17.en: We need delivery on Monday at 7 a.m.
17.note: Polite 필요합니다 form; casual crew talk can use 필요해요.

17.en: Can you deliver to the site at 123 Main Street?
17.es: 메인 가 123번지 현장으로 배송해 주실 수 있나요?

17.en: If the rebar doesn't arrive today, we can't pour concrete tomorrow.
17.es: 오늘 철근이 도착하지 않으면, 내일 콘크리트 타설을 할 수 없습니다.

18.en: The inspector arrives at 10, so let's finish cleaning up.
18.note: Casual-polite 해요-style would be 검사관님이 10시에 오시니까; 합시다 is a friendly crew-level suggestion.

18.en: Is the permit posted at the entrance?
18.note: Formal 입니까 suits talking to inspectors or site managers.

18.en: The rebar spacing is ready for inspection.
Please keep the scaffold area clear for the inspector.
18.es: 검사관이 볼 수 있게 비계 주변을 비워 주세요.
18.note: 주세요 is a polite request to crew members.

19.note: Use 작업자 for a worker; 근로자 is also common in formal or legal contexts.
Often just called 구급함 on sites; 구급상자 is the standard term.
Casual speech may use 기절. 실신 is clearer in an incident report.
Korea's emergency number for ambulance and fire is 119. Do not use 911 here; the script in the lesson uses 911 for the US.
Polite request to a coworker; 주세요 keeps it courteous.
Use 마세요 for a polite prohibition. Applies to any injured person.
Pressure on a bleeding wound; you must confirm the injury location with the worker first.

19.en: The first aid kit is over there.
Are you conscious? Can you hear me?
19.note: Check responsiveness before moving or treating; 정신 있으세요 is a natural check in Korean.

20.note: Common loanword in Korean construction; 점검 목록 is also understood.

20.en: Room 203 is missing the outlet cover.
20.note: Casual crew talk can drop 있습니다 to 있어요.

20.en: The crack in the drywall must be fixed before Friday.
20.es: 석고보드 균열은 금요일 전에 보수해야 합니다.

20.en: Who is fixing the door handle in the lobby?
The grout in the bathroom needs correction before the inspection.
20.es: 욕실 줄눈은 검사 전에 바로잡아야 합니다.

20.en: Please finish the touch-up paint by Thursday.
20.note: Polite request to a crew member.

21.en: Welcome. Let me walk you through the space.
21.note: Polite formal register, suitable for a client.

21.en: Here we installed the new tile flooring.
Do you have any questions so far?
21.note: Use 있으세요? or 있으신가요? both acceptable; 있으신가요? is slightly more formal.

21.en: Our warranty covers defects in workmanship for one year.
21.es: 저희 보증은 1년 동안 시공상의 하자를 보장합니다.
21.note: Confirm the actual warranty period from your company before using it.

22.en: The down payment is five million won.
22.note: Amounts in Korean can be spoken as 오백만 원 or written as 500만 원.

22.en: The balance is paid when the concrete pour is finished.
Could you send the invoice by email?
22.es: 청구서를 이메일로 보내 주실 수 있나요?
22.note: Polite form suitable for a client or owner.

22.en: Please transfer the payment to this account.
22.note: 입금 means depositing or transferring into an account.

23.en: Because of rain, we can't pour concrete today. We'll reschedule to Thursday.
23.es: 비 때문에 오늘 콘크리트를 타설할 수 없습니다. 목요일로 일정을 다시 잡겠습니다.
23.note: Polite formal register (-습니다) suits client calls and crew briefings alike.

23.en: Because of strong wind, we can't lift the rebar today. We'll reschedule to Friday.
23.es: 강풍 때문에 오늘 철근 양중 작업을 할 수 없습니다. 금요일로 일정을 다시 잡겠습니다.

23.en: If it keeps raining, we'll move the scaffold inspection to next week.
23.es: 비가 계속 오면 비계 검사를 다음 주로 옮기겠습니다.

23.en: The new expected completion date is March 20th.
23.note: Use 예상 완료일 for formal 'expected completion date'.

24.en: This corner is not at 90 degrees.

24.es: 이 접합부는 볼트를 더 넣어야 합니다.

24.en: This paint has bubbles. Please repaint it.
24.es: 이 페인트에 기포가 있습니다. 다시 칠해 주세요.

24.en: Please check this against the blueprint.
Can you fix this before the inspection?

25.note: Use 신입 for someone who just joined the crew.

25.en: First, watch me. Then you try.
25.es: 먼저 제가 보여 드릴게요. 그다음 해 보세요.
25.note: Polite 해요-style; suitable for a new worker.

25.en: Hold the board flat against the studs.
Do you understand the next step?
25.note: Use 이해하셨어요? to check understanding respectfully.

25.es: 좋아요. 이제 한 번 더 해 보세요.

25.en: Wear your hard hat and safety glasses.

26.en: In this team, we value respect for everyone.
26.es: 이 팀에서는 모두를 존중하는 것을 중요하게 생각합니다.
26.note: Polite formal register (-ㅂ니다), suited to crew speeches.

26.en: We do not tolerate shortcuts on safety.
26.note: Use 용납하다 for 'tolerate'; 허용하지 않습니다 is also natural.

26.en: Please help each other on the site.
26.note: -십시오 is a firm polite request, common for foremen.

26.en: Everyone must follow the safety rules.
If you see a hazard, tell me right away.
26.es: 위험한 것을 보면 바로 말씀해 주십시오.

27.en: Today we finished the rebar placement on level two.
Tomorrow we start the concrete pour at 7 a.m.
Before you leave, please return your hard hats to the rack.
27.es: 퇴근 전에 안전모를 걸이에 반납해 주세요.

27.en: Has everyone checked out, including the subcontractors?
Please leave the forklift keys at the site office.
27.es: 지게차 열쇠는 현장 사무실에 두고 가세요.

28.en: I listened to both of you.
The problem is the work schedule.
The solution is to switch shifts.
Let's keep the safety rules first.

29.en: This week we have a tough challenge: the concrete pour is due Friday.
29.es: 이번 주는 힘든 일정입니다. 금요일까지 콘크리트 타설을 끝내야 합니다.

29.en: I need each of you to check your PPE before every shift.
29.es: 여러분 모두 매 작업 전에 개인보호장비를 꼭 확인해 주세요.

29.en: If we work together, we will pass the inspection on time.
29.es: 우리가 함께 하면 검사를 제때 통과할 수 있습니다.

29.en: I understand your concern. Let's talk about it after the briefing.
29.es: 걱정되는 마음 이해합니다. 조회가 끝나고 같이 이야기해 봅시다.

29.en: Everyone, please meet at the scaffold at seven.
29.es: 여러분, 일곱 시에 비계 앞에서 모입시다.

30.en: Let's start the morning safety meeting.
30.note: Formal polite register (-ㅂ니다), suited to addressing a crew.

30.en: Everyone, please put on your hard hats and vests.
30.note: Polite request; 주세요 is standard on site.

30.en: Today's main hazard is the scaffold on the east side.
30.es: 오늘 주요 위험 요소는 동쪽 비계입니다.

30.en: Does anyone have questions before we start work?
30.es: 작업 시작 전에 질문 있으신 분 계세요?
30.note: 계세요 is the polite honorific form for asking a group.

30.en: Please finish the rebar work before the inspection.
30.es: 검사 전에 철근 작업을 마쳐 주세요.

30.en: Let's meet again at the end of the shift.
